title: Learning on Graphs with Out-of-Distribution Nodes

problem.claim: Graph learning must detect nodes with labels unseen during training and classify the remaining nodes into known classes.

gap.claim: Existing GNN research has paid little attention to graphs containing out-of-distribution nodes during training and inference.

contributions.claim: Defines graph learning with out-of-distribution nodes.
Proposes OODGAT, a GNN that models interactions between different node types and separates inliers from outliers during feature propagation.
Reports that graph connection patterns are informative for outlier detection.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe OODGAT as a novel GNN model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show OODGAT outperforms existing outlier detection methods by a large margin.
The authors report that OODGAT is better or comparable for in-distribution classification.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are established models for graph prediction tasks.
Graphs with out-of-distribution nodes have received limited attention.
The work formulates graph learning with OOD nodes as detection plus known-class classification.
The work introduces OODGAT and uses graph connections and node-type interactions for outlier separation.
Experiments report advantages in outlier detection and competitive in-distribution classification.

source_observation.claim: Graph connection patterns are reported to be informative for detecting outlier nodes.

interpretation.claim: Relational structure may provide useful signals for identifying distribution-shifted nodes.

application.claim: When designing graph anomaly detectors, consider structural relationships alongside node features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when connection patterns are insufficient or unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or training procedure in detail.
The abstract does not report computational costs, limitations, or reproducibility details.
